chapter: Jump for Joy and the Puerto Rico honour
title: Flamingo as an overture and Strayhorn's arrangement
summary: The band played Flamingo as the show's overture with Herb Jeffries singing, in Strayhorn's arrangement; Crosby was scared to cover it.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: Yeah, because there were a couple of pieces of music -- some of the music was recorded, and some of the music was not, and there were several numbers, like, do you remember a number called 'Flame Indigo'?
I know the only number I remember is the one that Jeff used to sing; we'd play an overture, and that was the main song we played -- da, da, da ...
'Flamingo.' Yeah. We used to play that as an overture, you know, and he used to sing it.
And that was a Billy Strayhorn arrangement, right?

I think that Duke told me that Billy Strayhorn's arrangement for Herb Jeffries of 'Flamingo' was the Renaissance of vocal arranging." He said that vocal arranging was never the same after Billy did that one for Herb Jeffries.

Oh, what was his name -- Duke asked Crosby to see if he could make a record out of it, and of course he told him that Jeffries had done such a good job that he was scared of doing any other version; that he could not make it any better than Jeffries', which he did do -- he really did a good job on that.

Yeah, he sure did. Another one, you know -- when Frank Sinatra did the album with Duke, and Frank sang 'I Like the Sunrise' from the 'Liberian Suite'? Al Hubler told me that Sinatra called him up and told him, 'I shouldn't have tried it -- nobody but you could sing it'.
